SILVER COULD HIT $75 AN OUNCE IN 2027, BANK OF AMERICA SAYS Bank of America (BofA) says silver could climb to $75 an ounce next year as macroeconomic headwinds ease. Silver closed Friday at $48.74, down 6.1% for the week, pressured by a stronger dollar, higher oil prices and Fed rate-hike expectations. BofA forecasts: 🔸 2026: 910-tonne supply surplus 🔸 2027: 852-tonne supply deficit Analysts expect ETF flows and solar demand to remain the biggest drivers of silver prices.

SILICON VALLEY VS. WHITE HOUSE: BATTLE FOR NVIDIA Tech executives are pushing to reinstate Jensen Huang, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly opposes his return. A petition backing Huang has drawn 175,000 signatures. Yet prediction markets give Huang just an 18% chance of returning as CEO, behind Rene Haas at 21%.
